projects.title: AI Cambrian
projects.summary:
A month and a half of running many agents in parallel, starting with Grokbot. OraXle and other projects grew out of it.

What hooked me was watching the bot work in its own computer's browser, on any website. Then there was voice mode connected to cloud agents that filed issues and worked overnight in parallel, not on my own hardware.

The loop that stuck was already there before, but now I could really lean into it: speak a milestone, then wake up to the overnight work waiting as a test release.

Around then I got into Lauren Tan's stack and her verification-first philosophy. Verifying is easier with an infinite token supply. Not easy, but easier, because you can stop, run the checks, and hand over the goal. If you define clearly what the goal is and how you'll know it's been reached, you don't need to stay in the loop. You can step out, as long as the verification is strong.

It ended when usage changed, with a shift to a hybrid stack around Hermes for control over spending and quick switching between providers. It's been an amazing journey, but if Grokbot keeps this usage pattern, it's not the solution, at least for me.

Takeaways:
- Go hybrid rather than all-in on new products.
- Experiment with them, and don't build everything on one.
- Infinite tokens made verification-first work possible, and with it, stepping out of the loop.
- Grokbot's current usage pattern isn't sustainable for me.
- I'm looking forward to the Hermes agent updates, especially the mobile app that's in the works.
